question: What does a fasting blood sugar test primarily measure?

options.B: Average blood sugar over the last three months
options.C: Blood sugar levels after not eating for a while
options.D: The highest sugar peak after a heavy meal

explanation: A fasting blood sugar test measures the amount of glucose in the blood specifically after a period of avoiding food, usually for eight to twelve hours. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h1)

question: Why is a fasting blood sugar test preferred over a random test for a clearer picture?

options.A: It is completely painless compared to other tests
options.B: It gives an accurate three-month average
options.C: It removes the sudden spike in sugar caused by recent meals
options.D: It requires no preparation from the patient

explanation: Fasting removes the temporary rise in blood sugar that happens right after eating, giving a stable baseline to work with. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h1)

question: Which hormone from the pancreas is released in higher amounts when a person is fasting?
explanation: Glucagon is released during fasting to help produce glucose and bring low blood sugar back up. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h2)

question: What is the main job of liver glycogen breakdown during an eight-hour fast?

options.A: Storing extra sugar as body fat
options.B: Turning dietary protein directly into energy
options.C: Releasing stored sugar to keep blood glucose stable
options.D: Stopping body tissues from taking up sugar

explanation: Glycogen breakdown in the liver releases stored glucose to supply the body when food is not coming in. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h2)

question: Which common symptoms often lead a doctor to order a fasting blood sugar test?

options.B: A dry cough and a mild fever
options.C: Severe joint pain and morning stiffness

explanation: Extreme thirst and passing urine very often are classic warning signs of high blood sugar that call for screening. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h3)

question: Why is a pregnant patient sometimes screened with a fasting blood sugar test?

options.A: To test for iron deficiency anemia
options.B: To check for high blood pressure

explanation: Routine screening helps catch gestational diabetes early, protecting the health of both mother and baby. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h3)

question: How long does a patient need to fast before a fasting blood sugar collection?
explanation: An 8 to 12-hour fast ensures that recent meals do not falsely raise the blood sugar reading. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h4)

question: Why must nurses check a patient's routine medications before a fasting blood sugar test?

options.A: Pills can physically damage the blood sample tube
options.B: Some drugs like steroids can alter blood sugar levels
options.C: All drugs cause severe nausea on an empty stomach
options.D: All medications must be stopped for a full week

explanation: Certain medications, such as corticosteroids, can raise blood sugar and give a false impression of the patient's health. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h4)

question: What fasting blood sugar level is used as a threshold to diagnose diabetes?
explanation: A fasting blood sugar reading of 126 mg/dL or higher on separate tests points to diabetes mellitus. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h5)

question: A patient's fasting blood sugar result comes back at 112 mg/dL. How should this be interpreted?

options.A: It points to prediabetes and means lifestyle changes are needed
options.C: It is a completely normal blood sugar level
options.D: It shows severe low blood sugar needing urgent care

explanation: Values between 100 and 125 mg/dL fall into the prediabetic range, showing a higher risk of developing full diabetes later. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h5)

question: How does sudden physical stress or trauma usually affect a patient's blood sugar?

options.A: It causes a sudden and permanent drop in sugar
options.B: It causes blood sugar to rise due to stress hormones
options.C: It keeps blood sugar at a normal baseline
options.D: It has no effect on lab values at all

explanation: Stress hormones like cortisol and adrenaline push blood sugar levels up, even when the patient is fasting. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h6)

question: Why can a delay in sending a blood sample to the lab cause a false test result?

options.A: Room temperature destroys all proteins in the sample
options.B: White blood cells create brand new sugar molecules
options.C: Oxygen gets into the container and evaporates the liquid
options.D: Red blood cells keep using up sugar inside the tube

explanation: Blood cells are still alive for a short time and consume glucose during transport, which leads to a falsely low lab report. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h6)

question: What is an important nursing action right after taking a blood sample from a fasting patient?

options.A: Throw away the sample if the patient feels weak
options.B: Check the puncture site and offer light snacks
options.C: Tell the patient to fast for another full day
options.D: Give a quick injection of rapid insulin

explanation: Checking the needle site stops bleeding, and giving food helps the patient recover their energy after fasting. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h7)

question: Which of these is a key responsibility for a nurse before doing a fasting blood sugar test?

options.A: Diagnose the patient just by looking at them
options.C: Make sure the patient actually followed the fasting rules
options.D: Calibrate the laboratory machines in the hospital

explanation: Nurses must confirm that the patient truly fasted so the lab results are accurate before the blood is drawn. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h7)
